FOREWORD This lndian Standard (Part I ) (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Solid Mineral Fuels Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related products Division Council. This standard was first published in 1966 and subsequently revised in 1977 based on ISO recollltlletldatiolls R 1213- i : 1971. lSO/R 1213-1 has been subsequently revised in 1982 and 1983 which is now available as IS() [2 13- I : 1993 `Solid mineral fuels -- Vocabulary -- Part I Terms relating to coal preparation'. The Committee, therefore, decided to revise this standard to incorporate more terlms. ISO 1213-1 : 1993 could not be adopted as Indian Standard since some of the terms have been modified from the definitions given in ISO and also a new term. namely, yield/relative density curve has been ordered which is not existing in ISO standard. `Hle composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A.

Indian Standard SOLID MINERAL FUELS -- VOCABULARY
PART 1 TERMS RELATING TO COAL PREPARATION

(Second Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard (Part 1) defines employed in coal preparation. 2 GENERAL 2.1 General Coal Preparation Terms by a Segregation -- Partial separation of a material into its constituents, occurring as a result of differences in particle characteristics, such as particle size or relative density. True Middlings; Bone -- Middlings homogeneous that their quality cannot improved by crushing and recleaning. 2.2 Cleaning Characteristics so nearly readily be terms commonly Recirculation -- The operation in which the whole or part of a product from a process is returned to the feed to a process, for example the return of the crushed overflow from a screen to the screen feed for rescreening. Reject; Refuse -- The material extracted from the feed during cleaning, for retreatment or discard.

Cleaned Coal; Clean Coal -- Coal produced cleaning process (wet or dry).

Coal Preparation -- Collectively, physical and mechanical processes applied to coal to make it suitable for a particular use. Coal Cleaning -- The treatment of raw coal to lower the quantity of undesirable constituents, through the difference in either density or surface properties. Discard; Dirt; Stone -- The material extracted from the raw coal and finally discarded. False Middlings; [nterbanded Middlings -- Middlings in which the particles consist of bands of coal and shale, and from which the coal may be liberated by crushing. Foreign Coal -- Coal received at a preparation plant from a source other than that to which the plant is attached. Imported country. Coal -- Coal coming from a foreign

Actual Performance Curve -- A performance curve showing the results actually obtained from a coal preparation treatment< Ash/Relative Density Curve -- The curve obtained from the float-and-sink analysis by plotting the ash percentages of successive fractions against the mean relative density of the fraction. Characteristic Ash Curve -- The curve obtained from the results of a float-and-sink analysis showing, for any mass percentage of floats (or sinks) the ash percentage of the highest density (or lowest density) fraction passing into these floats (or sinks), the mass percentage being plotted on the ordinate (vertical axis) and the ash percentage on the abscissa (horizontal axis). Cumulative Curve -- Any curve expressing the results of combining successive relative density fractions or size fractions. Cumulative Floats Curve -- The curve obtained from the results of a float-and-sink analysis by plotting the cumulative mass percentage of floats at each relative density against the cumulative ash of the total floats at that density. Cumulative Sinks Curve -- The curve obtained from the results of a float-and-sink analysis by plotting the cumulative mass percentage of sinks at each relative density against the cumulative ash of the total sinks at that density. 1

Low-G rade Coal -- Combustible material that has on Iy Iim ited uses owing to undesirable characteristics (for example ash percentage). Middlings -- A product of coal preparation that, because of its ash percentage, is intermediate between coal and discard.
NOTE -- [t follows, therefore, that the relative density of middlings is intermediate between those of coal and discard. Mi&llin&maybe reprocessed.

Run of Mine (ROM) Coal -- Coal produced mining operations, before screening, crushing preparation.

by or

Raw Coal -- Coal that has received no preparation other than possibly screening or crushing. Raw Coal Feed -- Raw coal supplied to a plant or machine, in which it undergoes some form of preparation.

IS 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Densimetric Curve; Relative Density Curve -- The curve obtained from the results of a float-and-sink analysis by plotting the cumulative mass percentage of tloats or sinks against the relative density. Expected Performance Curve -- A performance curve showing the expected results of a coal preparation treatment. Float-and-Sink Analysis -- The division of a sample into relative density fractions having defined limits, the amounts of the fractions being expressed as percentages of the total sample, commonly with an indication of the ash percentage (and other characteristics, if required) of each fraction. M-Curve; Mayer Curve -- A vectorial curve, obtained by plotting the cumulative ash percentages against their cumulative yields, used to express the washability of a coal, plotted on a vectorial diagram in which the projection of the vector on the ordinate (vertical axis) represents the percentage of the product (coal) and the direction of the vector represents the percentage of a particular constituent of the product. Near-Density Curve; Difficulty Curve -- The curve obtained from the results of a float-and-sink analysis, or from the densimetric curve, by plotting the mass percentage within the limits + 0.1 of a given relative density against that relative density. Performance Curve -- Any curve used to show the relationship between properties of coal and results of a specific treatment. of a coal to Washability -- The amenability improvement in quality by cleaning, generally through its relative density/ash relationship. Washability Curve -- Any curve obtained from the results of a float-and-sink analysis permitting the theoretical yield of floats or sinks to be read off.
NOTE -- curves: a) b) c) d) e)

Design Capacity -- The rate of feed at which specific items of plant must operate continuously and give the guaranteed results on a particular quality of feed. Equipment Flowsheet -- A diagram indicating, by standard symbols, the units of equipment used in the various operational steps carried out within a coal preparation plant. Feed -- Material appliance or plant. for treatment supplied to an

Liquids Flowsheet -- A flowsheet to indicate the flow of liquids throughout a series of operations. Materials concerned Flowsheet -- A flowsheet with solid materials. principally

Mechanical Maximum Capacity -- The highest rate of feed at which specific items of equipment, not subject to performance guarantees, will function on the type and quality of feed for which they are supplied. Nominal Capacity -- A notional figure, expressed in mass per hour, used in the title of a flowsheet and in the general description of a plant, applying to the plant as a whole and to the specific product under consideration. Operational Capacities -- Figures given on a flowsheet to indicate quantities per unit time passing various points in the plant, taking account of fluctuations in the rate of supply and composition (as to size and impurity content). Peak Design Capacity -- A rate of feed in excess of the design capacity that specific items of plant will accept for short periods with warranty without necessarily fulfilling the performance guarantee given in respect of them. Process Flowsheet -- A basic flowsheet indicating the main operational steps within the plant, the movement of the various materials between the steps and the final products obtained, and often also the average mass flow at various points in the plant. Weighted Flowsheet; Capacity Flowsheet -- A materials flowsheet used in the design of a plant, including statements of the mass flow per hour at principal points in the plant. 3 SIZING 3.1 General Classification -- The separation of particles according to their size, density and shape by control of their settling rate through a fluid medium. [S 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Fines -- Coal having a maximum particle size usually less than 3 mm, and having no lower limit.
NOTI; -- `i% upper limit may vary widely. To avoid confusion [he term shrruid always be qualified by stating the nominal size.

Effective Area (Screen); Working Area (Deprecated) -- The nominal area less any area occupied by fixings or supports that obstruct the passage of material over or through the screen deck. Fines Removal -- The removal of fine particles from a feed material, by either wet or dry methods, to facilitate treatment or utilization of the remainder. Misplaced Undersize -- Particles in a screen overflow that are smaller than a reference size. Misplaced Material (Screening) -- Undersize contained in the overflow, or oversize contained in the underflow. Misplaced Oversize -- Particles in a screen underflow that are larger than a reference size, Near-Mesh Material; Near-Size Material -- Material approximating in size to a reference size, usually within + 25 percent of that reference. Nominal Area (Screen) -- The total area of the screen deck exposed to the flow of the material feed, Open Area -- The ratio of the total area of the apertures to the total area of the wire cloth, perforated pIate or wedge-wire panel, expressed as a percentage. Probability Screening -- A method of screening that, by making extended use of the probability of a particle passing through an aperture, allows sizing at fine sizes to be performed with relatively large apertures. Scqeening -- The separation of solid materials of different sizes, by causing part to remain on a surface provided with apertures through which the remainder passes. Screen a) A device for carrying screening; and out the operation of

Mean Size -- The weighted average particle size of any salmple, batch or consignment of particulate material.
NOIE -- Several bases for calculating mean size have been proposed, giving results that vary widely for the same size distribution. The method of calculation should, therefore, always be stated whenever results are reported.

Nominal Size; Limiting Size -- The limit or limits of particle size used to describe a product of a sizing operation. Oversize -- Material in a product of size greater than the upper nominal size limit; may be expressed as a percentage of the product. Sizing -- Division of a material into products between nominal size limits. Size Analysis -- The process or the result of the division of a sample into size fractions, each within defined Iilmits, the mass or number of particles in each fraction being expressed as percentage of the total salmple. Sieve Analysis -- Size analysis in which the division is carried out by the use of test sieves. Smalls -- Coal having a maximum particle size usually less than 25 mm, and having no lower limit.
NOTE -- The upper limit may vary widely, To avoid confusion, lhe term should always be qualitied by stating the nominal size,

IS 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Wet Screening -- The screening of solid materials of different sizes with the aid of water. 3.3 Parts of Screens Loose-Rod Deck -- A screening surface consisting of loosely held parallel rods positioned at right angles to the flow of material over the screen. Relieving Deck -- A screen plate having large apertures mounted over the screening deck to reduce the load and wear thereon. Screen Deck; Screening Surface -- A surface provided with apertures of specified size for carrying out the operation of screening. Screen Plate -- A plate provided with apertures specified size and range for use as a screen deck. of Sizing Screen(s); Grading Screen(s), Classifying Screen(s) (Deprecated) -- A screen or set of screens normally used for dividing a product (for exaimple clean coal) into a range of sizes. Undersize Control Screen; Breakage Screen (Deprecated) -- A screen used for the removal or undersize from a product. 3.5 Screens According to Principle of Construction Bar Screen -- A stationary inclined screen, comprising longitudinal bars, spaced at intervals, onto which the material is fed at the upper end. Grizzly -- A rugged screen for rough sizing comparatively large size (for example >150 mm). at

NOTE -- A grizzly can comprise fixed or moving bars, discs, or shaped tumblers or rollers.

Screen Cloth; Screen Mesh -- A mesh of wires woven in a consistent manner to form the ape~tures. Wedge-Wire Deck; Wedge-Wire Sieve -- A screen deck, comprising wires of wedge-shaped cross-section spaced from each other at a fixed dimension, in which the underflow passes through an aperture of increasing cross-section.
NOTE -- Normally, a loose-rod deck is used only on high-speed vibrating screens.

Jigging Screen; Reciprocating Screen; Shaking Screen (Deprecated) -- A screen to which. a combined horizontal and vertical motion is imparted, normally by a crankshaft and connecting rod, the screen deck being horizontal or inclined at a smal I angle. Multi-Deck Screen -- A screen having two or more superimposed screening surfaces mounted rigidly within a common frame. Resonance Screen -- A screen having a period of oscillation at or very close to the natural period of oscillation of the resilient mounting. Rotating Probability Screen -- A device for probability screening, consisting of a rotating horizontal deck having radial spokes, the separation point being obtained by varying the rotational speed. Roll Screen -- A screen consisting of a number of horizontal rotating shafts, fitted with elements arranged to provide screening apertures. Single-Deck Screen -- A screen having one screening surface, not necessarily limited to one size or shape of aperture. Sieve Bend -- A device for the sizing of fine suspended in water by means of a stationary panel, usually of wedge-wire, the aperture of at right angles to the flow of feed, whereby particles are removed with the bulk of the the underflow. particles curved which is the finer water in

Dewatering Screen -- A screen separation of water from solids.

Deslim ing Screen -- A screen used for the removal of slimes from larger particles, usually with the aid of water sprays. Guard Screen; Oversize Control Screen -- A screen used to prevent the entry into a machine of coarse particle which can interfere with its operation. Primary Screen; Raw Coal Screen -- A screen used to divide coal (usually raw coal) into sizes more suitable for the subsequent cleaning of some or all of them. Rinsing Screen; Spray Screen -- A screen tfsed for the removal of fine solids by spraying, especially dense medium solids present among or adhering to larger particles. Run-of-mine Screen -- A screen used for dividing run-of-mine coal into two or more sizes for further treatment or disposal.
NO'TE -- A run-of-mine screen is usually employed to remove the Iargest pieces for crushing and re-addkion to the run-of-mine coal.

Trammel Screen; Revolving Screen -- A screen in which the screening surface is formed into a cylinder or frustum of a cone, mounted upon a horizontal or near horizontal rotating shaft, or on revolving rollers. Vibrating Screen -- A screen oscillated at high speed by either mechanical or electrical means. 4

Slurry Screen -- A screen used to recover and dewater granular products from circulating water in a coal preparation plant.

Classifier -- A device that separates particles, according to their size, shape and density, by physical means other than screening. Cyclone Classifier -- A device for classification by centrifugal means of fine particles suspended in a fluid, whereby the coarser particles are discharged tlom the apex of the vessel, and the finer particles are removed with the bu Ik of the fluid at the overflow orifice. 4 CLEANING 4.1 General Circulating Water -- The water in the water circuit.

Teeter (In); Fluidized Suspension (In) -- The condition of a suspension of solids in an upwardmoving current of water or air, whereby the support given to the particles reduces the internal friction between them to such an extent that the suspension acquires fluid or partially fluid properties. Wet Cleaning -- The mechanical separation of impurities from coal by methods involving the use of a liquid. Washery -- A coal preparation plant in which a wet cleaning process is carried out. Washery washery. Products -- The final products from a

Closed Water Circuit -- A water circuit designed so that the only water added is that necessary to replace the loss on the washery products and that due to atmospheric evaporation. Dry Cleaning -- The separation of impurities from coal by manual or mechanical methods that avoid the use ofa liquid. Froth Flotation -- A process for cleaning fine `coal in which the coaI, with the aid of a reagent or reagents, becomes attached to air bubbles in a liquid medium and floats as a froth. Head Tank -- A tank or vessel in the water circuit that is used to maintain the delivery pressure of the water by constant level to the washing units. Launder -- A trough or channel along which liquids or a mixture of liquids and solids flow. Middlings Elevator -- An elevator that removes middlings for further treatment or for disposal as an inferior product. Make-up Water -- Water supplied replace that lost from the circuit. to a plant to

Water Circuit -- The complete system of pipelines, pumps, sumps, tanks, launders and accessories used for the circulation of water in a washery. Waste Water; Surplus Water, Bleed Water (Deprecated) -- Excess water allowed to run to waste from the water circuit. 4.2 Dry cleaning Air Jig -- A machine in which the feed is stratitied by means of pulsating currents of air and from which the statified products are separately removed. Dry Cleaning Table -- An apparatus in which dry cleaning is achieved by the application of air currents and agitation to a layer of feed of controlled depth moved along the surface of the table, usually by a reciprocating action. Hand Cleaning-- The removal by hand of impurities from coal, or coal from impurities. Hand Selection -- The selection by hand of pieces of coal having certain specific qualities according to surface appearance. Picking Belt; Picking Table -- A continuous conveyor (for example in the form of a rubber belt or of a steel apron, steel plate or link construction) on which raw coal is spread for hand cleaning and/or hand selection. 5

Pump Sump -- A tank into which the process water gravitates and from which it is re-circulated by means of a pump. Pit Water; Mine Water -- Water from underground workings or an open-cut mine. Reject Elevator; Refuse Elevator (Deprecated) -- An elevator for removing and draining the reject from a washing appliance. Reclean; Rewash -- To re-treat a product in the same or in another plant.

Pneumatic current. 4.3 Jigging Air Pulsating Jig -- A jig in which the pulsating motion is produced by the intermittent admission of compressed air to the water, either alongside the jig bed, for example Baum, or under the jig bed, for example Batac, Tacub. Air Valve -- A valve that controls the alternate admission and release of compressed air to each cell of a jig. Bed Depth Transducer -- A device that measures variations in the thickness of heavy material on the jig screen plate without the use of a float. Diaphragm Jig -- A jig in which the pulsating motion is produced by the reciprocating movement of a diaphragm. Hutch -- The part of a jig situated below the jig screen plate in which the controlled pulsating movement of the water takes place. Feldspar Jig -- A jig used to clean coal usually smaller than 12.5 mm in size, in which the pulsating water is made to pass through abed of graded feldspar, retained on a compartmented jig screenplate. Float -- On certain types of automatic reject extractors, the part that detects variations in thickness of the layer of heavy material on the jig screen plate. Flushing materials Water -- Water used to assist the flow of in a chute or launder. Cleaning -- Cleaning by means of an air Jig Feed Sill -- That part of the jig over which the feed passes when it enters the box. Jig Centre Weir -- An adjustable plate situated between the feed end and the discharge end of a jig and serving to regulate the forward movement of material through the box. Jig Discharge Sill -- That part of the jig over which the cleaned coal passes out of the box.
NOTE -- Usually the discharge sill is part ot'the discharge end refise extraction chamber.

Jig Slide Valve; Jig Piston Valve (Deprecated) -- A jig air valve operated by means of a reciprocating motion. Jig Air Cycle -- The value-timing cycle determining the periods of air admission and exhaust. Moving Sieve Jig -- A jig in which the jig scree~ plate supporting the bed of material under treatment is moved up and down in water. Primary Jig -- In a series of jigs, the first jig, which receives the feed and from which one product at least is given further treatment. Plunger Jig; Piston Jig �A jig in which the pulsating motion is produced by the reciprocating movement of a plunger or piston. Primary Reject Elevator -- An elevator that extracts the first or more dense reject; usually situated at the feed end of the jig. Re-wash Jig -- A jig to which the product (or a portion thereofi of a previous cleaning operation is fed for additional treatment. Rotary Air Valve -- A jig air valve that rotates on a central axis, Reject Extractor -- A device used in a jig to remove the reject from the compartments of a jig, operated manually or automatically. Reject Extraction Chamber -- That part of the jig into which the reject extractor discharges. Reject Gate; Discharge Shutter (Deprecated) -- The mechanism of the reject extractor that may be manually or automatically operated to control the rate of removal of reject from the j ig. Reject Rotor; Star Wheel Extractor (Deprecated) -- A reject gate in the form of a rotary (or star) valve. Reject Worm -- A screw conveyor fitted at the bottom of some jigs to collect the fine reject which has passed through the apertures in the j ig screen plate. 6

Jig; Wash Box (Deprecated) -- A machine in which the feed is stratified in water by means of a vertical pulsating motion and from which the stratified products are separately removed. Jig Bed -- The whole of the material on the jig screen plate. 1S 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Reject Discharge Pipes -- Pipes used on some jigs instead of a reject worm. Secondary Reject Elevator -An elevator that extracts the second or less dense reject; usually situated at the discharge end of the jig. Top Water; Transport Water (Deprecated) -- Water introduced with the raw coal feed to assist the transport of material through the jig. Underscreen Water; Back Water (Deprecated) -- Water that is fed into the cells of a jig below the level of the jig screen plate. 4.4 Dense Medium Cleaning Circulating Medium -- Medium in circulation in or outside the dense medium separator, at or about the density of that in the separator. Dense Liquid -- greater than that of or in the laboratory of different relative A liquid or solution, of density water, that can be used in industry to divide coal into two fractions densities. Make-up Medium; Medium or medium replace losses. Make-up Medium Solids -- solids added to the circuit to

Magnetic Separator -A device for the recovery and concentration of medium solids that are magnetic. Magnetics -- The portion of the dense medium solids that has a high magnetic susceptibility and is therefore readily recovered by magnetic means. Medium Draining Screen; Depulping Screen (Deprecated) -- A screen for draining the separating medium from dense medium separator products. Medium Recovery Screen -- A screen for draining and spraying the product from a dense medium separator to remove adhering medium solids. Medium Solids Preparation -- Any grinding or treatment of the raw dense medium solids to make them suitable for use. Non-magnetics -- The portion of the dense medium solids that has a low magnetic susceptibility.
NOTE -- These solids are usually of lower relative density than the magnetics and are therefore classed as contaminants.

Dense Medium; Heavy Medium -- A fluid, formed by the suspension in water of particles of relatively high density (for example, magnetite, barytes, shale), that can be used in industry or in the laboratory to divide coal into fractions of different relative densities. Dense Medium Process -- A process for the cleaning of coal, in which the desired separation is effected in a dense medium. Dense Medium Separator -- A device, employing gravity or centrifugal force to effect separation, for the cleaning of coal using a dense medium. Dilute Medium -- Medium of density less than that in the dense medium separator, usually occurring as a resu It of spraying the products with water for the removal of adhering medium solids. Dense Medium Recovery; Medium Solids Recovery -- The cot Iection, for reuse, of medium solids from dilute medium, usually understood to include the removal, in whole or in part, of contaminating fine coal and clay. Dense Medium Plant -- A dense medium process including all the equipment associated with the recovery, regeneration and circulation of the medium. Device -- An automatic device to of the medium in, or entering, the dense medium separator.
the density

Over-dense Medium -- Medium of density greater than that in the dense medium separator, usually produced in the medium recovery system and used to maintain the desired density in the separator. Regenerated Dense Medium; Recovered Dense Medium -- Medium obtained from the medium recovery system and separated (wholly or partly) from contain in ants. Separating Medium; Correct Medium -- Dense medium of the density required to achieve a given separation. Suspended Matter -- Particles from the feed, of density equal or close to that of a separating medium, that are therefore relatively difficult to remove from the separator, because they are not readily recovered in either the float or the sink product. Shower Box -- A device that produces a continuous curtain of water droplets in a band over the full width of a screen; usually used on medium recovery screens. 4.5 Cleaning Equipment (Miscellaneous)

Dressing Water; Cross Water -- Secondary water used on concentrating tables. Hindered Settling Cleaner -- A wet cleaning device for fine coal, using a teeter bed combined with an upward current of water to effect separation. Plate Cleaner -- A device, for cleaning closely-sized raw coal, that uses the difference in the coefficient of resilience of friction between clean coal and an inclined plate, commonly of steel, and that between refLlse and the plate, to allow the clean coal to jump over a gap while the refuse falls through. Riffles -- Longitudinal strips of varying heights mounted on the deck of a concentrating table to separate the more dense particles. Trough Washer; Launder Washer -- A cleaning device applying the principle of alleviation in troughs. Upward Current Washer -- A washer in which separation takes place under the influence of an upward current of water or dense medium. 4.6 Froth Flotation Activating Agent; Activator -- A substance that, when added to a pulp, promotes flotation in the presence of a collecting agent. Selective Flotation -- A process for the preferential recovery of a particular ingredient of the coal, for example a metrological constituent, by froth flotation.

1S 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Wetting Agent --A reagent used to reduce the interracial tension between a solid and a liquid and therefore facilitate the spreading of the liquid over the solid surface. 5 SEPARATION OR AIR 5.1 General Centrifuging -- Dewatering centrifugal force. with the aid of Dredging Conveyor -- A scraper partially immersed in a vessel containing liquid and used for removing any solids that may settle therein, Dredging Sump; Drag Tank; Smudge Tank (Deprecated) -- A tank, forming part of the water circuit, in which slurry or small coal settles and is removed continuously by means of a scraper chain or scraper buckets. Fixed Screen -- A stationary inclined flat or curved panel, commonly of wedge-wire, that is used to remove a large proportion of water and fines from a suspension. Filter Bowl; Filter Tank -- A tank, containing the pulp to be filtered and generally fitted with an agitator to maintain the solids in the pulp in suspension, in which the drum or disc of a rotary vacuum filter is partially immersed. Filter Cloth -- A woven or felted fabric used as a medium for filtration. Filter Cake -- The solid product from the filtration process. " Filtrate -- The liquid product from the filtration process. Filter Press -- A form of pressure filter, noncontinuous in operation, used for the removal of water from slurries, tailings and similar products. Pressure Filter -- A filter in which filtration is carried out as a result of the application of pressure to one side of a filter medium. Solid-bowl Centrifuge -- A device for dewatering in which the retaining surface is imperforate, the retained solid particles are collected by a scroll and discharged from one end of the machine, and the water (centrate) overflows from the opposite end. Screen-bowl Centrifuge -- A dewatering device combining in one machine a bowl and a basket centrifuge. Vacuum Filter-- A filter in which filtration is carried out as a result of the application of a vacuum on one side of a filter medium. Filtration -- A process for separating solids from tiquids by allowing the liquid to pass through a finely woven cloth or gauze that retains the solids, using vacuum or pressure to accelerate the separation. Flocculation -- The formation of aggregates from particles dispersed in a liquid by the use of a flocculating agent. Plant Effluent -- Water, sometimes containing solids, discharged from a coal preparation plant, usually to waste. Slurry Pond -- A natural or artificial pond or lagoon for settling and draining the solids from washery slurry. Liberation (of Intergrown Constituents) -- Crushing of intergrown material to free the constituent materials. Reduction Ratio -- The ratio of the size of the feed to the size of product in a crushing operation.

Electrostatic Precipitator -- An apparatus for removing dust from dust-laden air, employing principle of electrostatic precipitation. 6 SIZE REDUCTION 6.1 General Breaking; Cracking (Deprecated) of large particles. -- Size reduction

Selective Crushing -- Crushing in such a manner as to cause one ingredient of the feed to be crushed preferentially to others. Selective Grinding -- Grinding in such a manner as to cause one ingredient of the feed to be ground preferentially to others. 6.2 Size Reduction Machines

Bali Mill; Rod Mill -- A cylinder, rotating on a horizontal axis, partly filled with balls or rods (generally of steel) that, by their tumbling motion, reduce a coarse material into a fine material by impact and abrasion.

10

IS 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Gyratory Crusher; Cone Crusher -- A machine in which the feed is delivered to a conical chamber in which a solid cone rotates eccentrically on a vertical axis. .Jaw Crusher -- A machine for reducing the size of materials by compression between a fixed plate and an oscillating plate, or between two oscillating plates, forming a tapered jaw. Pick Breaker -- A machine for breaking coal by the splitting action of mechanically operated picks. Rotary Breaker; Bradford Breaker -- A rotating, steel, perforated drum through which material of the desired size falls; the oversize material is lifted by flights inside the drum and falls back so that the weaker component (coal) breaks and passes through the perforations, whereas the hardest material (rock) remains unbroken and is rejected. Roll Crusher; Toothed Roll Crusher -- A machine in which size reduction is effected by causing the material to pass between a rotating roller, generally toothed, and a fixed or oscillating plate, or between two or more rollers. Rigid-Hammer Crusher -- A machine in which size reduction is effected by elements rigidly fixed to a rotating horizontal shaft mounted in a surrounding casing. Swing-Hammer Crusher; Swing-Hammer Mill; Swing-Hammer Pulverizer -- A machine ,in which size reduction is effected by elements loosely pivoted to discs fitted on a rotating horizontal shaft mounted in a surrounding casing. 7 EXPRESSION OF RESULTS is, material that has been included inthelower size or relative density product but that itself has a size or relative density above that of the cut-point, or vice versa.
NOTE --The mass of misplaced material maybe expressed as a percentageof the product or the feed.

Partition Curve; Distribution Curve -- A curve indicating the percentage of each density (or size) fraction contained in one of the products of the separation, Partition Coefficients; Distribution Coefficients -- The percentage of a particular density (or size) fraction recovered in one of the products of the separation. Statement of Performance -- A statement describing the scope and duty of a plant in terms, for example, of the tonnage of coal treated per hour, the processes used, the separations effected and the sizes produced.
NOTE -- A statement of performance can also be used to express the results of plant operation.

Total Misplaced Material -- The sum of the masses of the misplaced material in the products of a sizing or density separation, expressed as a percentage of the mass of the feed.
NOTE � If three products are made in a single separator, the total misplaced material will be the sum of the mass of material wrongly placed in each of the three products, expressed as a percentage ot' the feed to the sepamtor.

Total Correctly Placed Material -- The sum of the masses of material correctly included in the products of a sizing or density separation, expressed as a percentage of the mass of the feed to the separator (and equal to 100 minus the total misplaced material). Yield; Recovery (Deprecated) -- The amount of a product obtained from any operation, expressed as a percentage of the feed material. 7,2 Sizing Operations Control Size; Checking Size, Testing Size (Deprecated) -- A single size chosen to test the accuracy of a sizing operation.

Misplaced Material (Cleaning) -- Material of relative density lower than the separation density that has been included in the high density product, or material of relative density higher than the separation density that has been included in the low density product. Near-Density Material -- Material having a relative density lying between limits, usually 0.1, on either side of the cut-point. Organic Efficiency -- The ratio (normally expressed as a percentage) between the actual yield of a desired product and the theoretically possible yield (based on the reconstituted feed), both actual and theoretical products having the same percentage of ash. Partition Density (dp d5J; Tromp Cut-point -- The density corresponding to 50 percent recovery as read from a partition curve. Separation Density -- The effective. density at wh ich a separation has taken place, calculated from a relative density analysis of the products,
NOTE -- The separation density is commonly expressed as either the partition density or the equal errors density.

Ash Error -- The difference between the actual percentage ash of a product of a separation and that shown by the washability curve (based on the reconstituted feed) corresponding to the actual yield obtained. Correctly Placed Material (Cleaning) -- Material of reIative density lower than the separation density that has been included in the low density product, or material of relative density higher than the separation density that has been included in the high density product. 12

Sinks -- Fractions having a defined lower limit of relative density and so described, for example sinks at relative density 1.60. Theoretical Yield -- The maximum yield (as shown by the washability curve) of a product having a specified percentage of ash.

IS 3810 (Part 1) :2002 Yield Loss; Washing Loss (Deprecated) -- The difference between the actual yield of a product and the yield theoretically possible (based on the reconstituted feed) of a product having the same properties (usually percentage of ash). 8 MISCELLANEOUS Angle of Repose -- The angle between the surface of a heap of loosely piled material and the horizontal. Agglomeration -- A process in which tine particles are caused to adhere together to form balls or clusters, usually with the addition of a suitable reagent to promote adhesion. Blending -- Mixing in predetermined and controlled quantities to give a uniform product of desired properties. Bunker; Bin -- A vessel for the storage of materials, with the main section having vertical walls and the lowermost portion usually constructed in the form of a hopper. Bulk Density -- The mass in air of unit volume of bulk material, including the voids within and between particles. Dust-Proofing -- A surface treatment, for example with oil, calcium chloride solution or other surface active agent, to prevent or reduce the dustiness of coal in handling. Dust Suppression -- The prevention or reduction of the dispersion of dust into the air, for example by using water sprays. Freeze-Proofing -- A surface treatment, with reagents, to prevent or reduce cohesion of coal particles by ice formation during freezing weather. Hopper -- A vessel into which materials are fed, usually constructed in the form of an inverted pyramid or cone terminating in an openrng through which the materials are discharged (not primarily intended for storage). Paddle Mixer -- A horizontal screw conveyor having two non-continuous spirals which form paddles to propel and blend the constituents of the feed. Surge Hopper; Surge Bunker -- A hopper (bunker) designed to receive a feed at fluctuating rate and from which it is discharged at some predetermined rate. 9 BLENDING TERMS AND HOMOGENIZATION Core Flow; Funnel Flow -- Material flow, that is confined to a column immediately surrounding the vertical axis through the outlet and in which the material on the surface slides in towards the downward-moving column. Feeder -- A mechanical device for delivering material at a controlled rate. Heterogeneity -- The state of a material when particles having certain characteristics are distributed unevenly throughout it. Homogeneity -- The state of a material when particles having certain characteristics are distributed evenly throughout it. Homogenization material to obtain characteristics. -- The thorough mixing of a a product of relatively constant

Remote Indications -- The receiving and display of data at a point remote from the p~ocess or math inc. Remote Control -- The initiation of control operations for a process or math ine at a point remote from the motive power. The provision of equipment to enable plant and machinery to perform some or all of its operations without the intervention of an operator or attendant.

The process of comparing measured values with a reference value (set point) and correcting deviations from the reference value by automatic means.

NOTE -- Examples of the source or power are electrical,

Adaptive Control System -- A system in which automatic means are used to change the system parameters in a way intended to achieve the best possible performance of the system at all times. Alarm -- A visual or audible signal to attract human attention to a condition or state. Control System -- An arrangement of elements (for example, amplifiers, converters, human operators) interconnected and interacting in such a way as to maintain or to affect in a prescribed manner some condition of a body, process or machine that forms part of the system. Central Control -- The operation of a number of control functions on a plant from one central point. Data � Representation of facts, concepts or instructions in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation or processing by human or automatic means. Fail Safe -- A system concept in which the failure of any component or sub-system will not cause a hazard. Local Control -- Operator control of a plant from a position adjacent to the motive power. Manual Control -- The operation of a plant in response to command actions taken by an operator as opposed to those taken automatically. Management Information System(MIS) -- A computer system designed to acquire and retain information about the performance of operations and equipment, with facilities for retrieving that information on demand. 14

Ash Monitor -- A device that analyses coal quality in terms of ash percentage and produces a signal representing ash percentage. Analogue Computer -- A computer that uses physical quantities to represent numbers, for example, a pneumatic analogue computer uses pressure and flow rate, an electronic analogue computer uses current and voltage. Bulk Density Meter -- A device for monitoring the bulk density of a mineral to provide an indication of quality. Controller -- A piece of equipment that combines the function of at least the input elements, the comparing elements and the amplifying and signal processing elements, for a process control system. Converter -- A device that receives analogue signals in one form, for example pneumatic, and produces an equivalent output in another form, for example electronic.
NOTE -- A converter is usually qualitied by naming the types 01 signals received and produced.

Detector -- A device to indicate a specific occurrence. Density Meter -- A device for monitoring the relative density of a suspension. Dynamic Display -- A display by visual means that is effectively continuously updated so as to present up-to-date information at all times.

Limit Switch -- A switch that is operated by movement of a machine or apparatus beyond a set limit and that is frequently used to cut off power to the machine or to reverse its motion. Bureau of Indian Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau harmonious development of the activities of standardization, and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

of Indian

Standards

Act,

1986 to promote
of goods

marking

and quality

certification

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the Patestamendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc : No. PCD7(1837).
